runs.t: •  Understand a short local news report
•  Say what might or may happen
•  Ask Do you know where / when / why…?

slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive.
Point to the title and read it: "In the News" Say: "Understanding short local news reports and city notices: a road closure, a bus detour, a water pipe repair, a new bus route, a new store. Learners say what might or may happen and ask Do you know where / when / why…?. All stories, streets, and cities are invented and neutral."
Read the three lines under "Today you will".
Class stories only: all news is invented and neutral (roads, buses, a library, a store). No politics, crime, injuries, or real current events. If a learner brings up real news, say, "Let's keep to our class stories."
Lesson plan: Topic; At a glance: Objectives; Teacher notes.

slides.title: In the News

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these five things.
Every goal is a good goal.
I can understand the main points of a short local news report.
I can say what might or may happen, and what will happen.
Do you know where / when / why…?
I can tell a classmate about a local news story.
I can write a text or email (5–8 sentences) telling a friend the news.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Lesson plan: At a glance: Objectives.

slides.notes:
Step 3 · 6:15–6:30 · Listening + "Hear it, say it" · 15 min (slides 8 to 12). Individuals, then pairs check.
Before you listen (2 min). Say: "First, you'll hear a short local news report on the radio. Then two coworkers, Marco and Joy, talk about the news. Listen: what is the news?"
There are 3 people: Diane Lee, Marco and Joy. A narrator starts and ends the listening. Each click highlights the next person.
The audio (L4_L8_listening.mp3, about 1:50) plays the conversation once. Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer at a natural, friendly speed, two times. The script says going to and want to. People often say gonna and wanna; learners only need to recognize those words.
Audio: synthetic voices, computer-generated (Chatterbox TTS cloned from Kokoro-82M reference clips). No recordings of real people. The names and the story are invented.

runs.t: from a question to Do you know…?
Do you know where the meeting is?
Do you know when the bus leaves?
Do you know why the street is closed?

slides.notes:
Box 4: from a question to Do you know…? Each click shows the answer side of one row.
Questions and answers (2 min): Q: It might rains or It might rain? A: might + base verb: It might rain. Never -s, never to. • Q: Can I say Do you know where is the meeting? A: Use statement order: Do you know where the meeting is? • Q: will or might? A: will = I'm sure. might = maybe. The road will close on Monday. It might open early.
Check questions: "It might rains or It might rain?" (might rain) • "Do you know where is the bank or where the bank is?" (where the bank is) • "The sign says Closed Monday. will or might?" (will).
Lesson plan: Step 4; Grammar Box 4; Questions and answers.

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 7:00–7:15 · Talk Time: News Swap + What Might Happen? · 15 min.
Model it first (1 min): hold news card A. Ask a learner, "Do you know when the library will open on Sundays?" Help them find it and answer, "Yes, starting March 3." Then ask, "Do you know why?" Say: "Ask with Do you know…? Answer with a fact, or say I'm not sure. It might…"
Round 1 (7 min): News Swap (pairs). A and B have different news cards. Partners ask Do you know when / where / why…? and write the facts. Then they change partners and retell their partner's story. Each click shows the next step.
15 learners: pairs with one rotation for round 1; then groups of 4. 7–8 learners: pairs for round 1; then 2 groups. 5 or fewer: pairs for round 1 (you take a card if there is an odd number); then one group.
Lesson plan: Step 5; Talk Time: News Swap.

Round 2 (6 min): What Might Happen? (groups). Groups choose a headline and write 4 predictions with might, may, and will probably. Then they read them to the class. Each click shows the next step.
15 learners: pairs with one rotation for round 1; then groups of 4. 7–8 learners: pairs for round 1; then 2 groups. 5 or fewer: pairs for round 1 (you take a card if there is an odd number); then one group.
Every answer needs a reason; every partner asks a follow-up. Walk around and listen. Note 2 good sentences to praise and 1 common error for next week.
If behind: round 1 only.

Step 6 · 7:15–7:25 · Read & Write: A local news article · 10 min. Pairs read, then individual writing.
Read (4 min): Learners read the news article on the Read & Write page, find the main idea, and answer the questions. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers." Pairs answer questions 1–5 together.
Check (1 min): click to show each answer (one click per question, 1 to 5): 1 A new bus route, Route 9, will start on May 6. • 2 Every 20 minutes. • 3 $1.50 (and free for the first week). • 4 Sunday service. • 5 On the city website or at the library.
Write (5 min): Learners write a text or email to a friend about the news (5–8 sentences) with one might or may and one Do you know…?. Show the example. Learners start in class and finish at home (Homework item 2).

slides.notes:
Step 7 · 7:25–7:30 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket (3 min): learners open the Exit Ticket page and answer in 3 sentences with a reason: What might change in your neighborhood or at your job next year? Example on the board: A new store might open near my house. My job may change my schedule. I think so because there's construction on my street and my company is very busy. With 5 or fewer, a learner can say it to you first and then write it.
Collect the pages. After class, sort them into ✓ / almost / not yet. Start next week with 2 corrections on the board (no names).
Homework (2 min): open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (item 1: the store / may / open / in June → The store may open in June.). Say: "About 15–20 minutes. Finish your Read & Write writing at home."
Homework items: 1. Write the sentence or question. Use the words. • 2. Finish your writing from Read & Write C (your text or email). Read it one more time. Check ✓ the list in D. • 3. Write 3 things that might change in your neighborhood or city. Then write why you think so. • 4. Review (Lesson 7). Write one word.
Lesson plan: Step 7; Exit Ticket page; Homework page.
